events.open_questions: (1) Classification: S is chosen because the verifier's view of source-chain events was falsified while its keys were intact; a V reading (verifier operator infrastructure under unauthorized control) and a D reading (1-of-1 threshold set by the delegate) are both defensible. (2) Pause transaction hash and the two reverted delivery transactions were not found in sources read. (3) Adapter accounting is unclear: 223 rsETH left after the release, yet 40,373 rsETH were later held or withdrawn by Kelp; Aave's ARFC reads 152,577 rsETH as extracted, while LlamaRisk/Galaxy treat it as total L2 claims. (4) Whether the Arbitrum-frozen ETH has been transferred. (5) No source states whether the OFT adapter had a rate limiter configured.
